sql:
SELECT z.LocationID, z.Borough, z.Zone, COUNT(t.PULocationID) AS cash_trips
FROM ops.zones z
LEFT JOIN lake.trips t ON t.PULocationID = z.LocationID AND t.payment_type = 2
GROUP BY z.LocationID, z.Borough, z.Zone
ORDER BY z.LocationID

diagnosis.bottleneck: The query scans the entire trips table (495K rows) to filter payment_type=2, then hash-joins 99K probe rows to 265 zones with a per-row CAST, and finally aggregates; the dominant cost is the full scan and the join's type conversion.

plan_nodes.note: Join Type: RIGHT | Conditions: CAST(PULocationID AS BIGINT) = LocationID | Estimated Cardinality: 99167

hypotheses.claim: A filter on the joined side sits in the ON clause of a LEFT JOIN; the join dominates the cost. (matched: left join lake.trips t on … and t.payment_type = 2)
Full sequential scan of 495,833 trips rows to apply payment_type=2 filter; an index, zone map, or partitioning on payment_type could avoid reading non-matching rows.
The join condition CAST(PULocationID AS BIGINT) = LocationID forces a per-row cast on the probe side; aligning PULocationID and LocationID to the same integer type would eliminate this overhead.
The RIGHT OUTER JOIN probes 99,167 trips rows (only 243 distinct PULocationID) against 265 zones; pre-aggregating trips by PULocationID before the join would reduce probe volume and hash work.
